about: The public contract of the resource tools and of the twelve-tool surface as MDD-072 completes it: what each tool takes, in which unit each number is, how a page ends, which refusals exist, what an input may be and what a tool does not claim. The published input schemas and annotations of all twelve tools are the reference's (conformance/manifests/tools-and-options.json, artifacts/mdd-072/a0-probe/tools-list.json) and are unchanged; everything this file adds is an additional key of an answer. artifacts/mdd-072/twelve-tool-conformance.json is the evidence for it.

tools.open_dataset: opens DEX and APK paths; an archive without any DEX is a valid input: has_dex is false, dex_count 0, and the code tools refuse it (see no_dex)
tools.query: unchanged (MDD-042); on a dataset without DEX it is refused as no_dex, never answered with an empty result
tools.decode: unchanged (MDD-071); on a dataset without DEX it is refused as no_dex

modes.summary: the manifest, application and uses-sdk attributes, target SDK, component counts and the permission rows; offset and next_offset count permission rows, limit is rows per page (1..200)
modes.xml: the whole manifest as XML text; offset and next_offset count UTF-8 bytes of that text, max_bytes is 4096..131072 and a page holds at most a quarter of it

get_manifest.xml_text: the XML declaration, two spaces per level, an element with two or more attributes (namespace declarations count) one attribute per line, an empty element closed with />; every namespace declaration and every namespaced attribute is written under the prefix the document gave it; typed values are spelled out; text nodes are kept; a character XML 1.0 cannot carry (a control character other than tab, line feed and carriage return) and tab, line feed and carriage return in a value are written as character references; a value with an unpaired surrogate is refused, naming the attribute
get_manifest.value_spelling: integers decimal, hex integers as 0x and eight digits, booleans true/false, floats as the shortest decimal that reads back to the same f32 (inf, -inf, NaN), dimensions and fractions as mantissa times the platform's radix constant in f64 with the unit suffix (px dip sp pt in mm, % %p), colours as # and eight hex digits of the stored word, a reference as @ and eight hex digits (? for an attribute), null as <0xN, type Null>, an unknown type as <0xN, type Unknown(T)>, a dimension or fraction unit outside the platform's table as <0xN, type Dimension, unit U>
get_manifest.named_integers: installLocation, launchMode and protectionLevel (a flag word, highest flag first, joined by |) by their framework names; any other attribute stays a number, and a string-typed value is always its string
get_manifest.summary_and_xml_agree: the summary and the XML spell one value one way; the summary keeps characters exactly, the XML escapes them

get_manifest_components.rows: one per activity, activity-alias, service, receiver and provider under <application>, in document order
get_manifest_components.exported: the manifest's own android:exported when it is a boolean (reason explicit); otherwise the platform default at the target SDK: a provider is exported below API 17 (provider_target_sdk_default); a component without an intent filter is not (intent_filter_default); one with an intent filter is exported below API 31 (intent_filter_default); at API 31 and above, or with no target SDK, the state is null with the reason explicit_exported_required_or_target_sdk_unknown; an android:exported that is a reference this document cannot resolve is null with the reason exported_value_not_resolvable_here
get_manifest_components.exported_assumption: Android API 17+; manifest configuration only, excluding runtime state and permission checks
get_manifest_components.filters: kind (activity, activity-alias, service, receiver, provider) and only_exported (exported is true; null is not true)
get_manifest_components.paging: offset, next_offset and total_rows count components; offset == total_rows is an empty page, offset above it is invalid_range

list_resource_files.rows: every member of the archive, directory entries included, in name order (byte order of the stored name; the central directory's order breaks a tie, so members that share a name are all listed)
fields: raw_name_hex (only when the name is not UTF-8)
list_resource_files.paging: offset, next_offset and total_rows count members; rows are added while the answer fits max_bytes

formats.auto: Android binary XML as XML text (kind android_xml, same rendering as get_manifest xml), valid UTF-8 as text (kind text), anything else as lower-case hex (kind binary)
formats.hex: the stored bytes as lower-case hex (kind binary), for any member, a damaged binary XML included

read_resource.units: text and android_xml: offset, next_offset and page.total_bytes count UTF-8 bytes of the text shown, a page holds whole lines up to a quarter of max_bytes (a first line longer than that is cut at a character boundary and the page says ends_mid_line); hex: offset, next_offset and total_bytes count bytes of the member as stored, a page holds an eighth of max_bytes; source_bytes is always the member's size
read_resource.integrity: the bytes come from the dataset's own snapshot with the member's size and CRC-32 checked before any byte is shown; a failure is resource_error; source names the member (entry_index, member_id, content_id, sha256) and the snapshot
read_resource.cap: a member larger than 64 MiB (max_resource_bytes) is refused as quota_exceeded

query_resources.rows: one per resource and configuration, and for a map entry (style, array, plurals) one per item; the same resource in the default, en and zh-rCN configurations is three rows; configurations are never merged
fields: reference_id and reference_name (references and attribute references; reference_name null when this table does not define the id)
item_count, item_index, item_name, item_name_id, parent_id (map items)

filters.name: exact type/key, or package:type/key
filters.configuration: exact qualifier string; the empty string selects the default configuration only, leaving it out selects all

query_resources.configuration_strings: the platform's qualifier order: mcc, mnc, locale (en, en-rUS, b+sr+Latn+RS), ldltr/ldrtl, swNNNdp, wNNNdp, hNNNdp, small..xlarge, long/notlong, round/notround, widecg, hdr, port/land/square, ui mode, night/notnight, density, touch, keys, nav, WxH, vN
query_resources.references: named, not followed: reference_policy says so in every answer
query_resources.completeness: skipped_chunks counts chunks of a type the reader does not know and passed over by their size; it is 0 for a table read whole
query_resources.paging: offset, next_offset and total_rows count rows

errors.not_found: no member of that name; an archive without resources.arsc for query_resources; an archive without AndroidManifest.xml for the manifest tools
errors.invalid_input: the name is a directory entry
errors.ambiguous_input: several archives are open and input_index is not given; the answer lists archive_inputs
errors.invalid_range: an offset past the end, or inside a character of a text
errors.invalid_xml: Android binary XML that does not parse (read it as hex), or a manifest that does not parse
errors.invalid_resource_table: resources.arsc that does not parse; the table is refused whole, never read as far as it goes
errors.unsupported_capability: resources.arsc that uses what this reader does not read yet (a compact entry); the error says so, it is not called invalid
errors.resource_error: a member whose CRC-32 or decompression fails
errors.quota_exceeded: a resource over 64 MiB, a table over its budgets, an answer that cannot hold one row within max_bytes
errors.no_dex: query or decode on a dataset that has resources but no DEX
errors.argument_range: an argument outside its range (limit, max_bytes, kind, format, mode, resource_id above 32 bits) is a JSON-RPC invalid-params error; the reference answers an isError tool result

input_scope.resource_only_apk: opens (has_dex false); the resource tools read it; query and decode refuse it as no_dex
input_scope.no_resources_arsc: opens; list_resource_files and read_resource work; query_resources is not_found
input_scope.corrupt_resources_arsc: opens; query_resources is invalid_resource_table; read_resource reads the stored bytes
input_scope.bad_member: a member whose CRC fails is resource_error for that member only; the others stay readable
input_scope.strictness: a table with a wrong header type or a chunk reaching past its parent, binary XML with a namespace used but never declared, or with an attribute repeated on an element, is refused; the reference reads these leniently (declared)

not_claimed: names of the framework's own resources (android:attr/theme, @android:string/ok): ids of the framework are written as ids
the declared type of an attribute: only installLocation, launchMode and protectionLevel are given names
style spans of a pool string: the text is shown, the spans are kept in the parsed table only
compact resource entries (a table using them is refused as unsupported_capability)
overlays, staged aliases and library chunks beyond counting them in skipped_chunks
decoded resources (drawables, fonts, layouts as views): read_resource shows the stored XML, it does not inflate anything
runtime accessibility of a component, signature checks, the real default of a value a resource reference stands for

declared_differences.about: where this engine answers differently from the reference on purpose, found by replaying every recorded call (conformance/mcp/resources_replay.py); everything else is equal field by field

classes.ARGUMENT_RANGE_SHAPE: an argument outside its range is a JSON-RPC invalid-params error here, an isError tool result in the reference
classes.CONTROL_CHARS: the reference rewrites or drops control characters in attribute values; this engine keeps them exactly
classes.ENUM_ON_STRING_TYPE: the reference names a flag word from the data word of a string-typed protectionLevel; this engine shows the string
classes.ERROR_WORDING: both refuse with the same kind; the message is worded differently
classes.FRAMEWORK_NAMES: the reference names ids of the framework's own resources from an embedded table; this engine writes the id
classes.LIST_TABLES_SHAPE: list_tables answers objects here, names in the reference (declared in MDD-042)
classes.NAMESPACES_KEPT: the XML view here writes every namespace declaration and namespaced attribute under the prefix the document gave it; the reference writes the android namespace only, always as android
classes.ROW_BUDGET: the page ends one row earlier or later under a small max_bytes; the rows shown are the reference's rows
classes.STRICT_INPUT: a malformed input (wrong table magic, an AXML namespace not declared, a repeated attribute) is refused here and read leniently by the reference
classes.STRING_VALUE_AS_INDEX: in a layout the reference writes a string-typed android attribute as its pool index; this engine writes the string
classes.UNKNOWN_UNIT: a dimension or fraction unit outside the platform's table is written out in full here, as a bare number by the reference
classes.XML_TEXT_NODES: the XML view here keeps text nodes; the reference omits them
